# Independent audit of the shared ambient facet stress

Audited source: `candidate d485228e666ca27b`, together with its cited
finite affine-threshold saturation, compactness, compressed circuit, and
rotating-circuit notes.

## Conclusion

The owner-allocation objective, the two coincidence signs, the normalized
closed-cone separation, and the shared-body-plane moment equations pass
this audit under the hypotheses stated in the source. The note proves a
necessary finite-complexity stress certificate, not the missing multiplier
bound or OC.

Two notational conventions should be explicit when the argument is reused:
`cone(union G_j)` means the convex conic hull; and normalizing cap normals
requires rescaling their full inequalities and their positive circuit
weights consistently before freezing rho. The sign of the equality
multiplier q_i is chosen so that lambda_ij X_ij=rho_ij q_i.

## 1. Shared-representation closure

Unit continuous normals have a convergent subsequence. At a positive
limiting fiber their thresholds cannot tend to minus infinity, because
that fiber contains an interior ball eventually retained by all approximants.
The finite threshold limits lie in a closed finite affine-evaluation image.
The saturation lemma can preserve these finite values while raising the
other thresholds to redundant finite values at all other positive indices.

The source correctly proves that the finite limiting inequalities already
represent the entire limiting fiber, not merely its intersection with a
preselected ball: join an arbitrary feasible point to a fixed interior
point, obtain strict finite inequalities, and pass to the approximants.
The relaxed condition on zero-volume fibers is essential for this closure.
In the all-positive branch, small shared-plane perturbations preserve
positive bounded fibers and actual convex compatibility over fixed P.

## 2. Nonsmooth objective and compact allocation moments

At a coincident restriction, the intersection of the owner halfspaces has
outward first-order speed min_f r_f. Integrating the finite pointwise minimum
is exactly the minimum over measurable partitions of unity omega_f.
Pointwise first-owner tie breaking attains it. The resulting finite gradient
set is convex and compact: weak limits of the bounded allocation measures
retain domination and the partition condition, while masses and first
moments are continuous on compact facets.

Lower-dimensional face intersections and newly active constraints contribute
o(t) by finite-polytope swept-prism geometry. In d=1 the endpoint owners
are already full H_0 facets and are included explicitly.

## 3. Coincident cap signs and common trace requirements

For a body-inside-cap facet, the outward body normal is -u. In the u-normal
coordinate its new lower endpoints are -r for the body and -tau for the
cap; the intersection's outward change is min(r,tau). With owner speeds
this is min(min_f r_f,tau). Hence alpha_f>=0, sigma>=0 and
sum alpha_f+sigma=1 are exactly the relevant convex allocations.

For a body-outside-cap facet, the outward normal is u. The potential
intersection layer has length (r+tau)_+, giving
max(min_f r_f+tau,0). Its branch gradients lie in the stated convex set
sum alpha_f=sigma in [0,1]. This set may contain gradients not selected
by a particular direction, but its support function bounds the true
directional derivative above, which is all the separation argument needs.

The same alpha and sigma must enter both the body and cap-parameter terms.
The source enforces this. Its effective section measure equals ordinary
section area on proper cuts and sigma times facet area at coincidence.
These choices also agree with the divergence identities at inside and
outside coincidences.

## 4. Strict erosion and closure of the normalized cone

Common erosion makes every owner speed -1 and every cap-plane speed zero.
A positive-volume active cap contains a positive-area facet patch strictly
inside its open side. This patch gives a fixed negative contribution for
every cap-gradient allocation. Every other contribution is nonpositive.
Finitely many active caps therefore give one uniform strict negative bound.

If k_l=q_l+p_l converges in the stress cone, where q_l is a nonnegative
combination of cap gradients and p_l is polar, pairing with erosion bounds
the total cap coefficient from above. Compactness of each gradient set and
the finite cap list then yields a convergent cap part. The remaining polar
part converges in the closed polar cone. Thus the stress cone is closed.

Strict separation from the compact convex objective gradient set gives a
direction with every objective allocation positive and every cap-gradient
support nonpositive. Adding a small amount of erosion preserves the former
and makes the latter strictly negative. Actual one-sided derivatives then
produce a valid small competitor with larger total volume and all old cap
budgets strictly satisfied. This contradicts the attained extremal problem.
The resulting objective coefficient is one, not an abnormal multiplier.

## 5. Shared-plane and cap-side equations

With W_f=(omega_f-sum_j lambda_j alpha_jf)H_(d-1), independent variations
of b_f,a_f,n_f yield, respectively,

    integral W_f=0, integral z W_f=0, integral x W_f=0.

A redundancy among these equations caused by the plane equation is harmless;
free coefficient variations still imply them. No per-fiber equality or
pointwise equality of densities follows, and neither is claimed.

Writing the normalized identity as

    g0=sum_j lambda_j g_j-sum_(i,p)eta_ip D C_ip
          -sum_i q_i dot D(sum_j rho_ij u_ij)

gives the exact signs

    lambda_ij S_ij=rho_ij t_i,
    lambda_ij Z_ij=rho_ij sum_p eta_ip p,
    lambda_ij X_ij=rho_ij q_i.

The positivity of section mass at each deepest origin makes the nonzero
stress-group conclusions legitimate. Slack groups have zero cap multipliers,
and the threshold equation forces their coverage multipliers to vanish.

## 6. Homothety and its exact normalization

For joint continuous homothety, body a_f,b_f and cap v_j,b_j scale, with
continuous normals fixed. On each body facet r_f=n_f dot x for every owner.
On a cap boundary tau_j=-u_j dot x. At an inside coincidence n_f=-u_j,
so r_f=tau_j and every convex branch has the same value. At an outside
coincidence r_f+tau_j=0, again independent of the allocation. Proper
sections satisfy the ordinary divergence identity. Hence every objective
gradient has value dM and every cap gradient has value d mu(H_j).

The active homogeneous coverage constraints and continuous-normal equations
have zero homothety derivative. Therefore

    sum_j lambda_j=1/beta.

The source correctly stops short of an upper bound on each group's sum.
The new bulk-moment consequence, and the precise extra mixed moments for
n>0, are recorded separately in `candidate 3a33d309cb62f910`.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
